title: Rust retains only a short suffix of the input chain the Scala miner publishes
summary: With the Scala weak-blocks miner publishing an input block roughly every half second (initialDifficultyHex=4e20, subblocksPerBlock=64), the Rust follower never holds more than a couple of input blocks of the chain the miner has built. The blocks it does hold are byte-identical and on the same fork - `bestInputChain` is exactly Scala's list with the newest k entries removed, never a different history - so this is throughput, not a consensus divergence. It is recorded because the shortfall is large and steady, and because the disconnected waitlist overflows while it happens (`WaitlistFull`), which means announcements are being discarded rather than merely delayed.
not_a_divergence_because: every input block the Rust node did apply matches Scala's byte for byte, the chains never disagree about history (the smoke fails the run if they do), no DigestMismatch/TxDigestMismatch drop fired, the Scala peer was never penalised, and ordering-block heights stayed within 1.
next: re-measure against a release build before drawing any conclusion about the processor's throughput; if the shortfall survives that, the waitlist_entries bound and the per-announcement validation cost are the two things to look at.
